nodes.title: the Espadri signature
nodes.statement: The Espadri system concerns objects called wrenhobs. There are exactly 6 of them: iskglim, lornhob, tuisk, kaglim, xilfal, ovipyr. Two operations are written ; and |=. One relation is written >-, read as "dominates".

nodes.title: the Espadri combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x ; y for every pair of wrenhobs is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for |=. The pairs standing in the >- relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all wrenhobs x and y, x ; y is again a wrenhob.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all wrenhobs x, y, z: (x ; y) ; z = x ; (y ; z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all wrenhobs x and y: x ; y = y ; x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a wrenhob iskglim with iskglim ; x = x ; iskglim = x for every x.

nodes.title: an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a wrenhob ovipyr with ovipyr ; x = x ; ovipyr = ovipyr for every x.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all wrenhobs x and y, x |= y is again a wrenhob.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all wrenhobs x, y, z: (x |= y) |= z = x |= (y |= z).

nodes.title: self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: For every wrenhob x: x |= x = x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every wrenhob x: x >- x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all wrenhobs x and y: if x >- y and y >- x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all wrenhobs x, y, z: if x >- y and y >- z then x >- z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all wrenhobs x and y, at least one of x >- y and y >- x holds.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: For all wrenhobs x, y, z: if x >- y then (z ; x) >- (z ; y) and (x ; z) >- (y ; z).

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the second operation
nodes.statement: For all wrenhobs x, y, z: if x >- y then (z |= x) >- (z |= y) and (x |= z) >- (y |= z).

nodes.title: the system does not have reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: Some wrenhob x admits no wrenhob y for which x ; y and y ; x both land on a neutral object.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = lornhob, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every wrenhob x: x ; x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = lornhob, value = tuisk, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all wrenhobs x, y, z: if x ; y = x ; z then y = z.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = lornhob, y = xilfal, z = ovipyr, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all wrenhobs x and y: x |= y = y |= x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = iskglim, y = lornhob, left = lornhob, right = iskglim, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is no wrenhob that leaves every wrenhob unchanged under the second operation.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case reason = no two sided identity exists, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have spreading of the second operation over the first
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all wrenhobs x, y, z: x |= (y ; z) = (x |= y) ; (x |= z), and the same on the right.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = lornhob, y = iskglim, z = iskglim, left = lornhob, right = tuisk, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have the absorption pair
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all wrenhobs x and y: x ; (x |= y) = x and x |= (x ; y) = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = iskglim, y = lornhob, value = lornhob, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: drimi wrenhobs
nodes.statement: A wrenhob x is called drimi when x ; x = x.

nodes.title: wrenhobs that fexisk
nodes.statement: Two wrenhobs x and y are said to fexisk when x ; y = y ; x.

nodes.title: yukxil collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of wrenhobs is yukxil when x ; y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the solzam of a wrenhob
nodes.statement: The solzam of a wrenhob x is the collection of wrenhobs y for which x >- y holds.

nodes.title: the zamthra
nodes.statement: The wrenhob iskglim is called the zamthra of the system. It is the unique wrenhob that leaves every wrenhob unchanged under ;.

nodes.title: the vintvint
nodes.statement: The vintvint of the system is the collection of wrenhobs that fexisk with every wrenhob.

nodes.title: the lornglim
nodes.statement: The lornglim is the collection of all drimi wrenhobs.

nodes.title: the mimux of a wrenhob
nodes.statement: The mimux of a wrenhob x, written [x], is the smallest yukxil collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a nakgrix
nodes.statement: A wrenhob f is a nakgrix when f >- y holds for every wrenhob y, that is, when the solzam of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: muxtez wrenhobs
nodes.statement: A wrenhob x is muxtez when x ; x equals the zamthra.

nodes.title: the keldvash of a wrenhob
nodes.statement: The keldvash of a wrenhob x is the number of wrenhobs in its mimux [x].

nodes.title: the korrrast
nodes.statement: The korrrast of the system is the collection of wrenhobs whose keldvash is largest.

nodes.title: vorzel pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct wrenhobs x and y form a vorzel pair when x >- y and y >- x both hold, that is, when each lies in the solzam of the other.

nodes.title: the zamthra is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one wrenhob e with e ; x = x ; e = x for every wrenhob x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every wrenhob unchanged.
Then e ; f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e ; f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the zamthra lies in the vintvint
nodes.statement: The zamthra fexisks with every wrenhob.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the zamthra and x any wrenhob.
Then e ; x = x and x ; e = x.
So e ; x = x ; e, which is what it means to fexisk.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the vintvint.

nodes.title: the vintvint is yukxil
nodes.statement: If x and y both fexisk with every wrenhob, then so does x ; y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the vintvint and let z be any wrenhob.
Then (x ; y) ; z = x ; (y ; z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each fexisks with everything.
So x ; y fexisks with z, and the vintvint is yukxil.

nodes.title: the mimux of a wrenhob is yukxil
nodes.statement: For every wrenhob x, the collection [x] is yukxil.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under ;.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the mimux is contained in every yukxil collection
nodes.statement: If S is yukxil and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a wrenhob is drimi exactly when its keldvash is one
nodes.statement: x ; x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x ; x = x then {x} is already closed under ;.
So [x] = {x} and the keldvash is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x ; x, which is then x.

nodes.title: where the keldvash divides the number of wrenhobs breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every wrenhob x, the keldvash of x divides 6.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = lornhob, reach = 5, size = 6, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the mimux of a vintvint wrenhob stays in the vintvint
nodes.statement: If x lies in the vintvint then every wrenhob of [x] lies in the vintvint.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The vintvint is yukxil.
[x] is the smallest yukxil collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the vintvint is one.

nodes.title: the lornglim is yukxil
nodes.statement: If x and y are both drimi then so is x ; y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be drimi.
The claim asks whether (x ; y) ; (x ; y) returns x ; y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: solzams are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the solzam of x, then the solzam of y is contained in the solzam of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x >- y and let z satisfy y >- z.
Transitivity gives x >- z.
So every member of the solzam of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one nakgrix
nodes.statement: No two distinct wrenhobs can both be nakgrixs.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f >- h, since h is any object, and h >- f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the system has a nakgrix
nodes.statement: Some wrenhob nakgrixs the whole system.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: the relation survives combination on the right
nodes.statement: If x >- y then (x ; z) >- (y ; z) for every wrenhob z.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y lie in the solzam of x.
Compatibility applies the operation to both sides at once.
Nothing else is needed, since z was arbitrary.

nodes.title: no vorzel pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct wrenhobs lie in each other's solzam.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.

nodes.title: every wrenhob lies in the vintvint
nodes.statement: Every pair of wrenhobs fexisks.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The vintvint is defined by fexisking with everything.
The claim is that x ; y = y ; x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: where every wrenhob is drimi breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: x ; x = x for every wrenhob x.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = lornhob, value = tuisk, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where some wrenhob reaches every other breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: There is a wrenhob whose mimux is the whole system.

verification.domain: every object and its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case largest_span = 5, size = 6, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the relation reads the same in both directions breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: If x >- y then y >- x.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = iskglim, y = lornhob, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the zamthra swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e ; x equals the zamthra for every wrenhob x.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case anchor = iskglim, x = lornhob, value = lornhob, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the second operation keeps the vintvint intact
nodes.statement: If x and y lie in the vintvint then so does x |= y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The vintvint is already yukxil under ;.
The second operation is defined on every pair.
The claim is that |= respects the vintvint as well.
